title: Multiplying Fractions
short: Multiply the numerators and the denominators; an area model shows why.
trouble: Children find a common denominator first and keep it, so 1/2 × 1/2 comes out as 1/2.

blocks.html: You can find a fraction of a whole number. A fraction of a fraction works the same way: $\frac{2}{3} \times \frac{3}{4}$ means $\frac{2}{3}$ of $\frac{3}{4}$.
Multiply the numerators and multiply the denominators: $\frac{a}{b} \times \frac{c}{d} = \frac{a \times c}{b \times d}$. Then simplify. No common denominator is needed.

Shade $\frac{3}{4}$ of a square with 4 columns. Then shade $\frac{2}{3}$ of that part with 3 rows. The square is now cut into $3 \times 4 = 12$ equal pieces, which is why the denominators multiply. The double-shaded part is $2 \times 3 = 6$ of them, which is why the numerators multiply. So $\frac{2}{3} \times \frac{3}{4} = \frac{6}{12} = \frac{1}{2}$.

blocks.title: Half of a half
steps: Half of one half is a quarter of the whole.

blocks.title: A story
blocks.q: There is $\frac{3}{5}$ of a pan of lasagna left. Leo eats $\frac{1}{2}$ of what is left. What part of the whole pan does he eat?

blocks.html: Finding a common denominator first and keeping it: $\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{2}$. That treats multiplying like adding. Check: half of a half must be smaller than a half.
